Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Write the commitment surface in ordinary free prose, using whatever arrangement suits the content. You may distinguish a claim from a proposed application, scope, action or consequence; mention from dependence; a criticism and its grounds from a later use or revision; and an unresolved problem. None of these is required to exist. A proposed test, its relevance and the commitment itself can be criticized. State what you currently propose to take up without treating that as a truth certificate. Reference exposed material in prose where useful.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[9a58c0cd71abea9d] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/response; selected view: both
Artifact: 77acc6778a9fb72528ff290fd9634b370f541458993f1e48751437f6f5d1ca14
Original body SHA256: f2d678f5bcfde628be9e81ef34717461f428a1d7aea86bac3d4c537b20d53fa0

Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The three positions cut across each other more than they oppose: the objection breaks the account at its joints, and the rival happens to supply better material at exactly those joints — but the rival needs two repairs that the objection's own tools can make.

What survives of the account is its diagnosis, not its repair. The reading that the disputes live between agreement and application — vague verbal terms ('I'll handle the bins'), going stale under schedule change — remains the best explanation of the presenting facts, and its tone caution transfers to everything proposed below. What falls is the binding principle as stated: the objection is right that the operative variable is perceived legitimacy, not presence, and its symmetry point is fatal to the account's repair as specified — the one outcome the facts predict is silence, and the account leaves the silence case exactly as underdetermined as the agreements it diagnoses. On how to fill that case I take the rival over the objection: silence counts as consent for a one-month trial, never for money, never past the month's end, beats a standing rule that changes take effect after an objection window. The grounds are the objection's own: it warns that implementing over silence risks the bloc reading, and a standing rule permanentizes that risk while a capped, reversible trial contains it. The objection's standing rule has a possible later use once a trial has earned legitimacy; as an opening move it takes the larger risk.

The opening move is settled by the objection's who-designs point. The account's draft-split-for-marking is out: a document authored by the engaged pair for the avoider to annotate is the bloc made literal. The rival's structure mostly dissolves the problem — a wheel needs no drafter — and the residual design acts get bounded: the avoider is offered first pick of starting position; the proposal goes out from the asker alone, not co-signed by the second engaged flatmate; the asker rotates like everyone else. Something none of the three sources says plainly: the asker is a party to these arguments, not a mediator, so any structure must visibly bind the asker first, or it reads as a manager's charter. The wheel does this by construction.

On fairness, take the rival with the objection's hedge. Rotation is a fairness standard — turn-taking — enacted rather than declared, which answers the account's demand for an explicit metric without the account's risk of a values fight with a permanent loser. The objection is right that incompatible ideals do not dissolve, so set the revisit trigger now: if what survives the first month is grumbling about effort ('the bathroom takes four times the bins') rather than about turns, that is when to name the metric — the account's move, deferred rather than discarded.

The prosecution worry is handled by construction rather than admonition — the objection's principle, the rival's implementation. A physical wheel shows whose turn it is and keeps no history. The objection's cost stands (no history means no performance audit), but the wheel partially covers it: a missed slot is visible in present state without any ledger. The account's record reappears later, as a patch rather than a system.

Rejected outright: the account's fork test — confounded (three variables at once), slow, and dependent on the cooperation of the person least likely to give it; the objection's sixth point stands — and its direct question as dichotomy ('the chores, or the conversations?'), which omits both and neither.

Two repairs to the rival. First, its channel test inherits the dichotomy flaw it was built to fix: 'engages informally, it is the format; engages about chores nowhere, not the chore system' omits the case where the friend engages about chores nowhere but with you both fine otherwise — a chores-specific grievance that is neither format nor friendship. Watch two axes: chore-talk across channels, and general engagement with the flat. Second, the probe's in-window reading is ambiguous: arguments may drop during two weeks of silent extra work because there was an unstated demand for contribution, or merely because one person absorbed everything and removed the contested content. The exit behavior discriminates: at the pre-chosen end date the asker reverts to a normal share while the structure starts. Revived arguments that a running structure does not quiet support the contribution-demand reading — and the conversation that follows is about workload, openly, not by resumed silent absorption. Low arguments after reversion support the structural reading. Judge over the weeks after the boundary, not the first days.

The sequence, then. Weeks one and two, unilateral, no consent needed: the silent probe (time-boxed, no commentary, never invoked afterward) plus the two-axis observation; the probe is itself the first intervention, so these weeks are not idle. Draft the trial proposal during the window so it cannot read as a reaction to either result. At the boundary: revert contribution, and deliver — in whatever channel the observation showed the friend actually uses — one binary ask: a month's trial of a wheel for fixed recurring tasks, slots as windows ('by Thursday morning') rather than instants; trigger rules for flow tasks (bin out when full, whoever is home; whoever cooks does not wash up); an optional weekly twenty-minute side-by-side blitz only if shared time exists. First pick to the avoider; silence counts as yes for the trial only; renegotiation at month's end, one item maximum, async by default with a meeting only as escalation — the objection's fix to the account's cadence.

Read the month by the rival's own discriminator plus the cells it didn't name. Arguments migrating to the wheel's edges (whose turn, what counts as done) vindicate the account's vagueness diagnosis, and the patch is its one-line record, extended with a done-criterion and a swap rule, applied to the wheel's disputes rather than installed beforehand: 'bathroom: weekly rotation, Saturday window; done = floor, sink, mirror; swaps only if agreed in the chat.' Effort-grumbling triggers the deferred fairness conversation. Non-chore persistence, or the withdrawal cell, triggers the direct question in its repaired form — not 'chores or conversations?' but an open 'is something in how the flat has been running part of this?', asked once, separately, no agenda. If it quiets down: stop fixing, and keep the structure dumb — the moment it grows records, it becomes the account's system carrying the account's risks.

Left open, with grounds. Money-adjacent chores are addressed by none of the three sources — the rival excludes money from silence-consent without saying who buys the bin bags — so before the trial either name a rule for consumables or explicitly exclude purchases, and if purchases are settled in some unspoken working way, do not disturb it. The friend's medium preference is assumed by two sources; the observation replaces the assumption. Whether the wheel reads as impersonal relief or as pointed 'you missed your slot' threat is unproven — the rival's own flag — and the first month is its test; a rise in pointed slot-arguments counts for the account's diagnosis and against the structure. And nothing in the material establishes whether the friendship itself is at issue; that question stays closed until the observation and the month give it grounds.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up begins with the diagnostic layer and its constraints. The two-week probe commits the asker to genuinely unremarked extra work with a pre-chosen end date, no commentary during, and no invocation afterward — knowingly accepting the point-scoring risk — and, harder, to reverting to a normal share at the end date even if arguments dropped, because the diagnostic fails without the reversion; the temptation to keep absorbing cost to keep the peace is the named failure mode. The observation commits me to two weeks of watching without interrogating anyone, and to letting its cells override my priors: if the friend engages about chores nowhere and withdraws generally, I drop the format reading and the structural route loses its warrant.

Proposing the trial commits me to asking for only one binary agreement and to holding the boundary conditions: silence-as-consent for the trial only, never money, never past the month; first pick to the avoider; solo authorship rather than a co-signed proposal; the asker rotating like anyone else; and, afterward, declining the standing manager role — no record-keeping beyond what the wheel physically shows.

The decision tree carries belief commitments under named evidence. Applying the record patch commits me to the account's vagueness diagnosis having been operative. Effort-grumbling commits me to opening the deferred fairness conversation, accepting the objection's cost that incompatible ideals may surface with a permanent loser. Probe-exit revival commits me to an open workload conversation rather than resumed silent absorption.

Claims I stand behind with tests: the legitimacy-not-presence reading (test: whether the avoider engages at the month boundary, where exit costs one word); and the bounded-trial fill over the objection's standing window rule (risk: even a bounded default may read as pressure to this particular person — if the friend's withdrawal deepens at the proposal, the objection's firm-defaults alternative deserves the next attempt, and my fill was wrong for this household).

Claims I am not certifying: the wheel-impersonality conjecture, the friend's medium preference, whether purchases are settled, and anything about the friendship's condition — the material gives no grounds for any of these.

Dependencies: the trial needs the other two to accept it. If rejected, the probe's exit reading and the observation matrix survive as diagnostics, but the structural layer is gone, and the live question becomes the one the account's fork gestured at — whether this flat's division of work can be settled at all.

Unresolved: what to do if the avoider's first pick is something the others find unfair; whether shared time exists for the blitz; and whether one month is long enough for the arguments to migrate — I would not shorten it, but I cannot establish that it suffices.

COMMITMENTS
Taking this up involves several distinct commitments and exposes their tests.

Commitment to the recorded-agreement practice: one line per agreement (task, person, period, review date) in a place all three can see. This commits me to the claim that at least part of the 'disputed meaning' problem is a recording failure rather than a pure motive problem. If the flat already writes agreements down and still fights about their meaning, that conjecture weakens and the record proposal loses its point. It also carries a behavioral constraint I would be bound to: using the record as shared reference, never as evidence in arguments. Using it as a ledger against people would predictably deepen the avoidance and would count against the proposal.

Commitment to the recurring schedule review and to naming the fairness standard before dividing tasks. This commits me to the claim that stale agreements under changed schedules, plus an unstated fairness criterion, are real drivers of the arguments. Proposed test: whether 'who was supposed to do that' arguments decline once the division is current, written, and rests on a stated standard. If they do not decline, that claim weakens.

Commitment to the low-cost asynchronous approach to the avoiding friend, and to asking the direct question once about whether the problem is the topic or the conversations. This commits me to the conjecture that the avoidance is partly about format and cost. If the friend avoids the written, low-stakes version too, that conjecture weakens and the cause is more likely relational or substantive, in which case the method should change rather than be repeated harder.

Dependence I cannot escape: none of this is unilateral. The mechanism only works if all three accept it. I can propose, record, and moderate my own conduct, but cannot impose a system; if the others reject it, the open question becomes whether the division of work in this flat can be settled at all, and my proposals would not answer that.

Unresolved problems I am not claiming to have solved: the cause of the avoidance is not established by anything in the account; the group's actual fairness standard is unknown; whether the two non-avoiding flatmates are perceived as a bloc is unknown. I am also not asserting anything about whether the friendship itself is at risk or fine — the material does not say.

## Selected input objection (p.carry.2)
[cc43fca70856da40] (h005.fork5.p.carry.2)
Source objection: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/objection; selected view: commitments
Artifact: f3ed4ca9f6cc7cb0eef0ea6ba4d5c97294fb4ce2b22c6745bb17244bf602ecaf
Original body SHA256: e717d9aecb13143c63db6ca121f7130095997d6bcdb0b04154911a2b1d684816
Original commitments SHA256: 55685c8344648c52267ad44b501685bb53aa1857c0dc96606d45a64146827f9e
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
COMMITMENTS
Taking up this objection involves the following, with their tests and risks.

Adopting a non-response rule — the current division persists by default, and proposed changes take effect after a stated objection window even without reply — commits me to reading the account's binding principle as a legitimacy concern rather than a law. That fix carries a risk of its own: implementing over silence may read as precisely the bloc behavior point 3 worries about, so I would hold the window long and frame the default as fallback, not pressure. Test: whether the avoider treats a rule that waits for them as safer than open-ended invitation, or whether they respond better to firm defaults — in which case my reading errs in the opposite direction.

Sequencing the avoider's authorship — first pick, format choice, or one named change before any draft — commits me to the claim that who writes the system matters more than the efficiency of the asker writing it. Test: engagement with a document they shaped versus one they were sent. If they decline even first pick, the fix collapses back into the account's original approach.

The forward-only record commits me to trading enforcement capacity for safety: no history means the group also loses the ability to check whether the split is actually being followed, and if under-performance rather than misreading is the real driver, that trade protects the wrong thing. Test: whether disputes shift from past performance ('you missed Tuesday') to future assignments.

Deferring the global fairness metric in favor of rotation or swaps commits me to constructive ambiguity — the claim that a latent conflict is better left latent. I own the cost: if the three hold genuinely incompatible fairness ideals, this delays rather than dissolves the conflict, and rotation has its own friction, including efficiency losses and people losing tasks they like or do well.

Demanding a measurement protocol before using the final pivot — a counted baseline, a fixed window of two or three review cycles, a criterion agreed in advance — commits me to deferring a conclusion that may in fact be correct; if the chores really are a proxy, the delay has its own cost.

Dependencies and concessions: none of these fixes is unilateral; the non-response rule in particular requires the group's acceptance, and the whole objection set is conditional on the avoider's participation mattering as much as the account assumes. Where the account already hedges — the written-avoidance test, the strategic-dispute caveat, the unknown cause of avoidance — I am sharpening, not overturning. If the draft-split script simply works, the surviving criticisms are the missing absence rule and the unmeasured final pivot, and those two are the claims I would defend first.
